hard_case: Measured defect (#7715): ripr reported the related test's oracle `assert!(results.iter().any(|r| matches!(r, Ok(_))))` as exact_value / strong, because any `matches!` text in the condition credited it whatever its pattern. RIPR-SPEC-0231 rule 3 (example 7 is the same `Ok(_)` pattern as the whole condition): the nested `Ok(_)` only checks the side of some element, so it pins no value and the test reads no stronger than a bare `assert!`, relational_check / weak. The line verdict stays gap; the overclaim showed in the related test's reported oracle. Since #7715's fix ripr reports relational_check / weak.

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: check(5) returns Ok(6); Ok(_) accepts it
not equivalent: check(5) errs, so no element matches Ok(_)

reasoning: assert!(results.iter().any(|r| matches!(r, Ok(_)))) over [check(5)] only checks the Ok side: Ok(x + 1) passes, Err(E::Bad) fails. The nested pattern pins no value.
